newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady but at higher range.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady but at higher range.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges moved up in late trade on Tuesday to the higher range of Monday's trade, defying expectations the market would soften due to weak demand.
High sulphur cargoes were offered steady to slightly weaker, but could draw support from low avails, and one percent was unchanged with a balanced supply/demand picture.

A major bought some 2,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel barges at $85 fob Rotterdam in the afternoon, or at Monday's highest level, after earlier buying at $84.75. Early in the day Antwerp barges traded at $84.50.
Monday's low trade level was $83.25 to $84 late in the day.
Some traders said the market would fall with demand seen low, and some added later that the late deals were just an attempt to drive the market higher.
"They're trying to keep prices up but this will not hold, demand is low," one trader said. He put total bunker demand at 10,000 tonnes.
But the major said its buying was genuine physical need.
Low sulphur barges were quiet, with buyers and sellers still far part and supply and demand said to be balanced.
